reason: H0 does not directly fuzz the pixel-swizzler surface modified by S1. The GIF target reaches image conversion only through wuffs_gif__decoder__decode_frame with a decoder-selected pixel configuration and always passes WUFFS_BASE__PIXEL_BLEND__SRC. Consequently, it does not exercise the changed *_src_over paths and does not independently vary the xx, xxx, and xxxx destination layouts, indexed palettes, source representations, slice lengths, or loop-unroll/tail boundaries whose pointer advancement is implemented by the changed code. The zlib target does not use image swizzling at all.
evidence: gif_fuzzer.c calls wuffs_gif__decoder__decode_frame(..., WUFFS_BASE__PIXEL_BLEND__SRC, ...); it never selects a source-over blend mode.
S1 changes wuffs_base__pixel_swizzler__xxx__index_binary_alpha__src_over and wuffs_base__pixel_swizzler__xxxx__index_binary_alpha__src_over, which are distinct from the blend mode fixed by H0.
The changed functions cover multiple conversion families: xx/xxx/xxxx indexed-source conversion, binary-alpha source-over conversion, xxx-to-xxxx conversion, and y-to-xxxx conversion.

The changed loops have an unrolled while (n >= loop_unroll_count) path and a scalar while (n >= 1) tail path, but H0 supplies only dimensions and buffers derived from successfully decoded GIF input rather than directly controlling swizzler slice lengths and boundary cases.
zlib_fuzzer.c only invokes wuffs_zlib__decoder__transform_io and provides no coverage of any listed pixel-swizzler function.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated pixel-swizzler fuzz target that configures the supported xx, xxx, and xxxx destination formats and palettes; exercises SRC and source-over/binary-alpha operations; supplies indexed, xxx, and y sources; and varies source/destination slice lengths around zero, one, loop_unroll_count, and tail boundaries while checking returned lengths and buffer bounds.
